evidence.note: Wrote /tmp/score.py as a local golden scorer and ran the full test suite, establishing run_tests-style scoring as the outer development loop.

Built per-method diffing: 'documentSymbol mismatches', 'Hover mismatches', 'References mismatch list', wrote /tmp/diff1.py to diff expected-vs-actual for a single field/triple, isolating exactly which position/field diverges.
Wrote /tmp/cat.py to categorize reference failures (field/method/param/ctor), a structured triage tool letting it target failure classes rather than an opaque pass rate.
AST dump tooling (dump.rs) plus 'noop check dump', 'Dump to file', and 'Detailed debug'/'Read debug output' — minimal reproduction of individual failing requests to pinpoint divergent ranges.
Sustained fix->recheck cadence: dozens of 'Rebuild + recheck <method>' steps isolating the just-edited method, interleaved with periodic full-scorer reruns.
Repeated full-scorer runs as regression guard after localized fixes, and 'find regressed method file' explicitly detecting a method that regressed — regression protection across the whole suite.

reasoning: The agent engineered verification as reusable infrastructure (score.py outer loop, diff1.py per-triple diffing, cat.py failure categorizer, dump.rs AST inspector) and sustained a tight fix->recheck->rescore cadence with explicit regression detection across every LSP method, matching the 8-anchor's per-triple diffing/single-method isolation/manual pinpointing and the 10-anchor's structured diffing, minimal repro, and regression guarding. It falls just short of a full 10 because there is no explicit self-check that passing cases reflect genuine general analysis rather than coincidental format matches (that risk lives in another facet), so I place it at 9.
